subject: Parity offer — takeover credits vs platform fit
messages:
From: Sophia Li <sophia.li@trellis.ai>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Evan Park <evan.park@trellis.ai>
Date: 2027-05-02T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Exploring parity with our current vendor (pricing + integration ask)

Hi Alex —

Thanks for taking the time on the call earlier. Quick follow-up from our side: Trellis is evaluating a vendor swap and our CFO asked if Redwood can match the effective economic terms our incumbent (NimbleCloud) is offering. Key asks from Evan/finance: a 12-month effective price parity, a one-time migration credit to cover integration effort, and clear runtime compatibility notes for our vector pipeline (long tail sequence lengths, 8K average).

Can you share what a parity offer would look like (credits vs % off ARR) and whether there are any technical caveats we should budget for? Evan copied on thread for numbers.

Best,
Sophia Li
Head of Product Partnerships
Trellis AI

Attachment: incumbent_term_summary.xlsx (stub)

From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
To: Sophia Li <sophia.li@trellis.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-03T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Exploring parity with our current vendor (pricing + integration ask)

Sophia —

Appreciate the context. Quick summary of what we can do and the open items:
- Pricing parity: we can equalize unit economics via a blended package: a 6% per-token effective discount for the first 12 months combined with a $150k migration credit applied to the first invoice. Alternatively, we can offer a 12% upfront commit credit (prepay) that nets to similar economics depending on your usage profile — I'm including both options in the attached PDF.
- Credits vs discount: credits are more flexible for one-off integration services; a % discount is simpler for long-term unit cost. We generally prefer a hybrid (small credit + moderate discount) for mid-market swaps.
- Technical caveats: our runtime supports continuous batching and prefix caching. For Trellis's 8K average sequence lengths we recommend the quantization profile Q4-B and a dedicated pool for initial 3 months to stabilize latency. We'll include an integration checklist and a short-run performance test plan.

I've attached a draft parity offer (trellis_parity_offer_v2.pdf) and an integration_checklist.xlsx. Could Evan share an anonymized usage curve (monthly tokens by model) so we can refine the numbers? Marissa, Rishi — looping you in for concession guidance and SLA exceptions.

Next steps: Evan -> usage curve; Redwood -> final pricing and scoped migration credit statement.

Thanks,
Alex Martinez
Account Exec, Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachments: trellis_parity_offer_v2.pdf (stub), integration_checklist.xlsx (stub)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>, Sophia Li <sophia.li@trellis.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-04T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Exploring parity with our current vendor (pricing + integration ask)

Alex / Sophia —

Quick note on the concession framework from a retention perspective:
- Migration credit composition: we typically split credits into two buckets — onboarding services ($75k, fixed) + usage credits ($75k, burn against normalized token billing) to align incentives.
- Timeline: credits tied to a 90-day onboarding milestone (50% on initial model uplift, 50% after production cutover).
- Rollback protection: include a 30-day rollback SLA where Redwood will provide reduced-rate fallback to the incumbent model for any regression (limited to 2% of requests/day).

On integration: for your pipeline we recommend an initial 2-week perf validation window on a dedicated cluster and then a staged ramp. Rishi, can you confirm whether the dedicated pool will require a separate commit or can be billed against the same reserved capacity?

Marissa Cole
Head of Growth 
Redwood Inference

Date: 2027-05-06T10:38:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Exploring parity with our current vendor (pricing + integration ask)

Thanks — Evan attached the usage curve (monthly_token_curve.csv) and added a few clarifying points:
- Migration credit: Trellis prefers credits applied directly to invoices rather than vendor-paid professional services.
- Integration risk: our infra team flagged concerns around KV cache compatibility and warm-start latency for long tail queries. We need the perf validation to include cold-start and 95th latency across our 8K samples.

On credits vs discount: Evan says a blended approach is fine if the migration credit is invoice-applicable. Also, can Redwood commit to a 6-month price floor after year one if we sign a 24-month contract? That's a major sticking point for procurement.

Sophia

Attachment: monthly_token_curve.csv (stub)

Date: 2027-05-09T16:44:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Exploring parity with our current vendor (pricing + integration ask)

Sophia / Evan —

Thanks for the curve and the clarifications. Final proposal (summary):
1) Credits: $150k total applied to invoices (split 75k onboarding services + 75k usage credit that offsets token billing). Credits expire after 12 months.
2) Discount: 6% effective per-token discount for first 12 months.
3) Commit & Floor: 24-month term with a 6-month price floor after year one (no unilateral increase >3% during floor).
4) Technical & Validation: 2-week perf validation on dedicated cluster (no separate committed capacity required for the validation cluster; billed against usage), and an SLO for 95th pct latency target we will codify in the SOW. Rollback protection as Marissa outlined.
5) Onboarding milestones: 50% of onboarding services credit released after performance validation, remainder after production cutover.

If this aligns, we'll update the offer PDF and SOW and route for signatures. If you prefer a larger upfront commit credit instead of the usage credit, we can run that sensitivity once you confirm expected monthly token mix.

Alex Martinez
Account Exec, Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference
